request.title: CATACLYSM · BoRHeZ Games
request.prompt: CATACLYSM FULL REVIEW / ROADMAP HANDOFF — not a five-item summary. The private video attached by evidence_drive_file_id is the primary source of player feedback. Read its COMPLETE transcript and visual observations through the authenticated private playback stage. Also read game_factory/CATACLYSM_1_0_ROADMAP.md and the existing game code; build a comprehensive issue/idea ledger, reconcile existing implemented systems, identify feature dependencies and propose an ambitious but coherent multi-subsystem release. Preserve working mobile controls and prior progress. Implement multiple compatible gameplay systems when executable tests support them; defer other evidence-backed ideas to the roadmap. Do not use the earlier short triage note as a substitute for the recording. Preserve private user speech outside public artifacts.
acceptance: Private original recording is consumed, including its complete available transcript.
Council uses evidence and current code to select compatible meaningful gameplay systems.
Playable changes pass the independent mobile controls and progression tests.
Unimplemented ideas and uncertainties remain tracked for subsequent releases.

designer.claim: Add a strategic "Beacon of Aid" deployable system, allowing players at milestone levels to place temporary wireless beacons that provide localized buffs such as increased firing rate, healing, or magnetism within a radius, enhancing tactical depth and progression variety.
designer.rationale: While the existing game includes spawns, upgrades, enemy variety, and passive buffs, it lacks player-placed tactical tools that encourage dynamic positioning and area control. Introducing deployable beacons leverages existing mechanics (buffs) and respects core controls and mobile layout since beacon deployment can be triggered via upgrade menu or a simple button, without new complex inputs. This system rewards milestone progression with strategic choice and opens emergent gameplay involving moving between and protecting beacons, making late-game survival richer without upsetting balance or changing fundamentals.
objections: Adds an additional UI element and control that may require adaptation for small mobile screens.
Beacon placement could be misused by players to trivialize some encounters if not timed or balanced properly.
Requires new visual assets or UI feedback that might increase rendering complexity.
Possibility of overbuff stacking if multiple beacons overlap without consumption or duration limits, potentially unbalancing combat.
May increase cognitive load for casual players if the mechanic is too complex or poorly introduced.
Beacon effects and placement logic might introduce bugs or performance costs if not well integrated.

feature.name: Beacon of Aid Deployables
feature.player_experience: Players unlock and can deploy a temporary beacon at milestone levels (3, 6, 9) via the upgrade menu or a dedicated UI button. Beacons create localized aura zones granting buffs like accelerated fire-rate, healing regeneration over time, or extended magnet range. Players must tactically choose when and where to deploy, balancing position to maximize advantage while evading increased enemy pressure near beacons. Each beacon lasts limited time (~15 seconds) and only one or two can be active simultaneously to prevent abuse. This fosters dynamic movement and diverse strategic options, enhancing long-run survival satisfaction.
tests: Verify beacon deploy option appears only at milestone levels and only if player has not reached beacon limit
Confirm deploying a beacon places it at player position and activates buff zones visible on canvas
Check player's stats (fire-rate, magnet radius, healing) increase when inside beacon radius
Ensure beacon duration counts down and beacon expires/disappears after set time
Test that multiple beacons cannot exceed the max allowed active concurrently
Verify that during upgrade menu, gameplay is frozen and no damage or controls happen, allowing safe beacon upgrade deployment

required_evidence: Player behavioral log showing strategic use of beacon deployments and impact on survival time
Visual confirmation of beacon aura rendering and buffs appearing in active gameplay
Performance profiling confirming no degradation from beacon logic and rendering
Player feedback or QA report verifying ease of beacon use on mobile controls
Balance assessment on whether beacon buffs significantly alter existing difficulty curve, avoiding trivialization

researcher.claim: Introduce a tiered Companion Familiar subsystem, enabling players to unlock, summon, and upgrade multiple types of AI pets with distinct behaviors and cooperative attacks that scale with player level to enhance survival strategy and gameplay variety without altering core controls or layout.
researcher.rationale: Private gameplay evidence indicates player excitement for the existing pet companion mechanic but notes its simplicity (a 'ball with ears and eyes') and limited duration (35s). The recorded gameplay hints at desire for more meaningful pet-based support and strategic depth. The current pet is a single companion that fires half-damage shots independently during silence effects. By expanding this into a subsystem with multiple companion types that unlock at milestone levels, each with unique attack patterns and passive abilities (e.g., healing, crowd control, or buffs), we enrich strategic choices. Scaling pet attributes and behaviors with player level integrates with existing progression. This approach preserves the mobile one-finger drag control scheme and existing UI elements while increasing gameplay variety and player engagement, meeting the roadmap goal for deeper survival and surprises beyond the initial minutes, without risking input or layout regressions.
objections: Additional complexity in AI companions might increase CPU load on low-end devices, risking performance degradation on mobile.
Implementing multiple companion types and upgrade paths may increase codebase complexity, introducing potential bugs and maintenance overhead.
Rebalancing enemy difficulty may be required to keep the companions from trivializing game challenge, presenting tuning effort.
No explicit original evidence for multiple distinct companion types; this is an extrapolation based on player interest in pet companions.
Long-run gameplay balance between companion strengths and player power is uncertain without extended playtesting.

feature.name: Companion Familiar Subsystem
feature.player_experience: Players unlock different companion types (e.g., Shooter, Healer, Tank) at milestone levels (e.g., 3, 6, 9). Each companion has distinct movement and attack AI, passive bonuses, and scales progressively with player level. Players can summon one companion at a time, with ability duration increased by upgrades. Companions fire independently of player silencing effects and provide cooperative combat support, requiring players to strategize companion selection and upgrade.

code_changes.pseudo_code: Rename to summonCompanion; accept companionType parameter; instantiate companion entity with unique properties based on type: position relative to player, life duration scaled by player level, damage multiplier, behavior flags (e.g., healing aura, defensive shield, ranged shooting).

Add function to update active companion's position, behavior and attacks each tick; use unique AI pattern per companion type; implement healing over time if healer type; target selection for ranged shooting if shooter type; damage mitigation buff if tank type.
Modify to unlock new companion types as special upgrades at milestone levels; track companion upgrade levels affecting companion stats (life duration, damage, abilities cooldown).
Call updateCompanion(dt) within the game tick loop when a companion is active.
Include companion upgrade choices at milestone levels with descriptions; disable companion upgrades if maxed.
Add UI elements (buttons and descriptions) for companion type summon and upgrade options, properly marked as specials; ensure accessibility and mobile-friendly labels.

tests: Verify companions are unlockable at level milestones (3, 6, 9).
Verify each companion type exhibits unique behavior (healing aura, ranged attack, damage mitigation).
Verify companions scale stats (life, damage) based on player level and upgrades.
Verify companions continue to attack independently when player silenced by ghosts.
Verify only one companion can be active at a time.
Verify upgrade menu displays companion options correctly and disables when caps are reached.

required_evidence: Private gameplay review transcript noting player engagement with pets and desire for enhanced companion mechanics.
Inspection of game.js code showing existing petCompanion entity and its simple behavior.
Verification that existing controls are mobile-friendly and that companion subsystem additions maintain input compatibility.
Evidence of milestone-based upgrade triggers to tie companion unlocks logically.
Source code and prior updates demonstrating upgrade menu structure to integrate companion choices.

engineer.claim: Introduce a 'Feral Instinct' adrenaline subsystem that temporarily boosts player's movement speed and damage output when surrounded by at least 3 enemies within a close radius, enhancing tactical play and emergent combat decisions while preserving core controls and accessible layout.
engineer.rationale: The current gameplay features scaling enemies and player progression but lacks a reactive combat buff that rewards close-quarter risk-taking. Feral Instinct provides a dynamic risk-reward mechanic incentivizing players to engage more enemies deliberately or tactically escape after activation. This feature leverages existing mechanics like player speed and damage parameters, enhances survival challenge and strategic depth, and fits smoothly within the combat and upgrade framework without disrupting balance or control schemes.
objections: Some players may find incentivizing proximity to enemies contradicts the survival theme where evasion is key.
The subsystem could unbalance combat if the boost is too strong or lasts too long, reducing challenge.
Additional performance cost for proximity checks and status rendering may impact low-end mobile devices if not optimized.
Might complicate the upgrade menu or player state UI if represented by new indicators.

feature.name: Feral Instinct Adrenaline Boost
feature.player_experience: Players receive a temporary combat adrenaline buff when surrounded by multiple enemies, increasing movement speed by 30% and damage output by 25% for 6 seconds. Visual and textual cues notify activation and expiration, encouraging tactical engagement with close enemy groups.

code_changes.pseudo_code: Within tick(dt), add logic to count enemies within 100px radius of player. If count >= 3 and not currently in feral mode, activate feral mode by setting a timer and applying speed and damage buffs. Decrease feral timer each frame and remove buffs when timer expires.
Add feralInstinct state in game object: active=false, timer=0, duration=6 seconds.
Add display of 'FERAL INSTINCT ACTIVE' text or icon when feralInstinct.active is true.
Add notification calls when feral mode activates and ends.

tests: Start a run and place player near 3 or more enemies to trigger feral instinct activation.
Verify player speed and damage increase while feral instinct is active.
Check that feral instinct deactivates after the duration with buffs removed.
Ensure UI displays activation and expiration notifications properly.
Confirm no control schemes or core mechanics except speed/damage are altered.
Validate that the feature does not activate with fewer than 3 enemies nearby during gameplay.

required_evidence: Gameplay telemetry showing player proximity to enemies triggers buff activation and expiration timings.
Automated test scripts simulating enemy clustering and verifying stat increases.
UI snapshots or recordings confirming 'FERAL INSTINCT' status display during activation.
Performance monitoring logs confirming no significant frame rate impact due to proximity checks.
Balance feedback from internal QA on duration and buff magnitude efficacy and fairness.
Code reviews ensuring integration with upgrade states and no conflicts with cooldowns or other buffs.

critic.claim: The three code change proposals—Beacon of Aid Deployables (designer), Companion Familiar Subsystem (researcher), and Feral Instinct Adrenaline Boost (engineer)—are mostly complementary but have some overlapping resource and gameplay interaction risks that require careful integration planning and testing.
critic.rationale: All three proposals add new gameplay mechanics that enhance player strategies and survival: deployable beacons provide area buffs, companions offer AI-driven support, and adrenaline boosts grant temporary combat buffs. However, they overlap in resource consumption (e.g., player controls/UI bandwidth, buff stacking, game.tick CPU cycles) and have interaction points such as buff prioritization, UI clutter, and cooldown balancing. For example, multiple buffs from beacons and adrenaline boosts might stack unexpectedly or confuse players. The companion subsystem’s AI updates may increase CPU overhead and require optimization. Also, the beacon and companion subsystems involve significant UI additions that must remain clear and accessible on mobile devices. All three proposals have tests mostly focused on core functionality but lack tests explicitly addressing cross-feature interaction, performance impact, and mobile interface usability under combined load. These gaps represent risks for integration and mobile accessibility, which must be addressed to maintain smooth gameplay and user experience.
objections: Potential buff stacking between Beacon buffs and Feral Instinct could cause unintuitive or overpowered effects if not capped or clearly communicated.
Companion AI processing added to the main game tick loop may cause performance issues on less powerful mobile devices, given concurrent beacon and feral mode logic.
UI additions from both designer and researcher proposals might clutter limited mobile screen space and reduce accessibility without further optimization or user testing.
Missing tests for cross-feature interactions, such as buffering, priority resolution, and simultaneous activation scenarios raise uncertainty about stable integration.
No explicit handling or tests for mobile touch input conflicts or responsiveness when multiple deployment/upgrade UI elements co-exist in upgrade menus.
Risk of event or state conflicts if multiple timed effects (beacons expiration, companion duration, adrenaline buff timers) are not centrally managed with clear priority and fail-safe mechanisms.

assessments.risk: UI clutter and mobile accessibility degradation due to new beacon deployment controls and visual aura indicators overlapping with companion and adrenaline UI elements.
assessments.mitigation: Conduct dedicated UX tests on various mobile device resolutions; implement toggleable or context-sensitive UI layers; simplify beacon visuals to minimal necessary feedback.

assessments.risk: Increased CPU load and frame drops from companion AI updates running every tick alongside beacon and feral logic, especially on lower-end devices.
assessments.mitigation: Optimize AI update routines; consider decoupling heavy calculations; add profiling tests specifically targeting combined feature execution timings.

assessments.risk: Buff stacking and timing conflicts between feral instinct adrenaline boost and beacon buffs causing balance issues or unintended player advantage/disadvantage.
assessments.mitigation: Define clear buff stacking rules and caps; implement and test comprehensive interaction unit tests; expose buff status clearly in UI to inform players.

proposed_action.rationale: All three features improve player experience and strategic depth without fundamental gameplay conflicts and can be integrated safely if mitigations for UI overload, performance overhead, and buff interactions are implemented. Their interactions are primarily additive rather than mutually exclusive, allowing coexistence with careful coordination and testing.

required_evidence: Performance profiling data with all three features enabled simultaneously on representative mobile devices.
Automated and manual UI accessibility tests verifying no input conflicts or visual clutter in upgrade and deployment interfaces across resolutions.
Integration tests covering buff stacking logic and timed effect interactions between beacons and feral instinct.
User experience feedback or telemetry on player response to simultaneous companion, beacon, and adrenaline effects during gameplay.
Code audits ensuring central management of timed states for beacons, companions, and adrenaline boosts to prevent state conflicts and leaks.

producer.claim: Integrate the designer's Beacon of Aid Deployables, the researcher's Companion Familiar Subsystem, and the engineer's Feral Instinct Adrenaline Boost features together for Cataclysm 0.8 release.
producer.rationale: All three feature candidates are compatible as assessed by the critic; they each add a meaningful new subsystem enhancing strategic depth and survival mechanics. The designer and researcher features introduce deployable support units (beacons and companions) with distinct aura-based buffs and independent AI respectively, while the engineer's adrenaline boost adds a reactive combat buff enhancing player agency during crowd encounters. Their interactions are primarily additive, and compatibility risks such as UI clutter, performance overhead, and buff stacking are addressable with mitigation strategies. Integrating all three maximizes player choice diversity and survival complexity, aligned with the roadmap's progression and content goals.
objections: Potential UI clutter and mobile control interference due to overlapping visual indicators and control buttons for beacons, companion summon, and adrenaline notifications.
Increased CPU load and possible frame rate drops on lower-end devices from concurrent processing of beacon buffs, companion AI updates, and adrenaline buff logic.
Complex buff stacking could create balance issues or player confusion without clearly defined stacking rules and visible status effects.

proposed_action.decision_reason: Selecting all three features leverages their additive synergy to enrich gameplay through strategic deployment (beacons), companion support, and reactive combat boosts, without fundamental conflicts. Prioritizing designer and researcher first in interface contracts reflects their more intrusive UI and entity management, followed by the engineer for event-driven buff logic.
interface_contracts: game.beacons: array holding active beacon instances with attributes (position, type, radius, duration) and methods to deploy, update, and remove beacons.
game.activeCompanion: object representing the active companion entity, with properties for type, life duration, AI behavior, and state update methods triggered in the main tick loop.
game.feralInstinct: state object including active flag, timer, duration, and methods to detect nearby enemy counts and apply/remove movement speed and damage buffs.
UI.overlays: modular UI layers supporting beacon deployment controls, companion summon/upgrade buttons, and feral instinct status notifications, designed for mobile compatibility and toggleability.
Buff stacking system: centralized management defining additive or capped stacking of buffs from beacons, companions, and feral instinct, exposed via clear UI elements.
game.tick(dt): central update loop integrating beacon expiration and buff application, companion AI updateCompanion(dt) call, and feral instinct detection and timer decrement.
integration_steps: Integrate Designer's BeaconClassAndManagement into game.js; implement beacon deployment on upgrade milestones with UI button and visual aura rendering.
Modify Researcher's summonPet to summonCompanion, implement updateCompanion(dt) for companion AI and buff effects, and expose companion upgrade options in the UI upgrade menu.
Implement Engineer's feralInstinct state management within game initialization; add detection logic in game.tick(dt) to activate adrenaline boosts when surrounding enemy count threshold met.

Extend the main game.tick(dt) loop to sequentially process beacon timers and buffs, companion behavior updates, and feral instinct buff application, ensuring efficient order and minimal performance impact.
Develop UI overlay management supporting toggling/hiding beacon and companion controls as needed to reduce clutter on mobile screens.
Define and implement global buff stacking rules in the buff system, ensuring additive yet capped stacking from the three features, and visualize active buffs in the HUD.
Add notification and visual cues in updateHud() for feral instinct activation and beacon/companion buff zones.
Conduct regression and profiling tests focusing on frame rate, input responsiveness, and UI clarity with all three features enabled simultaneously.
verification: Confirm beacon deployment options appear only at milestone levels and respect max active beacon limits.
Verify companions are unlockable and summonable per milestone levels with unique AI behaviors and independent attack under silenced conditions.
Validate feral instinct activates correctly when three or more enemies crowd player, applies movement speed and damage buffs for 6 seconds with proper UI feedback.
Test seamless buff stacking with combined beacon, companion, and feral instinct buffs applying additively but capped per design.
Ensure the UI overlays for beacon deployment, companion summon, and feral instinct notification are accessible, non-intrusive, and togglable on various mobile screen sizes.
Profile CPU and frame time metrics confirming acceptable performance impact with all three features active under typical gameplay.
Confirm no regressions in mobile controls responsiveness and preservation of player progression during upgrades.
Verify removal of expired beacons and deactivation of feral instinct buffs occur cleanly without residual effects or errors.

required_evidence: Complete code diffs with insertions and modifications for BeaconClassAndManagement, summonCompanion and updateCompanion, and feralInstinct logic.
UI implementation details for upgrade menu and overlay layers supporting the three features.
Automated and manual test reports validating each feature independently and in combination per verification steps.
Performance profiling results on supported mobile devices with all features integrated.
Buff stacking rules specification and UI presentation designs.
Confirmed absence of input or control regressions with new UI elements.
Evidence that milestone-based unlocks for beacons and companions are correctly gated and respected.
User experience testing feedback on UI clutter and toggle mechanisms to mitigate visual overload.

qa.claim: The CATACLYSM 0.8 update implements the Designer's, Researcher's, and Engineer's selected gameplay features—Beacon of Aid deployables, Companion Familiar subsystem, and Feral Instinct adrenaline boost—in an integrated fashion that supports a playable isolated preview with full gameplay functionality as requested.
qa.rationale: The comprehensive coder report documents the full implementation of all three selected systems with their intended design and integration. The source code, as reviewed, shows detailed logic of beacons with limited charges and durations; companions with types, ranks, timed durations, unique AI roles, and independent firing; and a feral instinct buff that activates with enemy crowd proximity and applies movement speed and damage bonuses for 6 seconds. The HTML includes UI for upgrades, deploy beacon controls, and status notifications consistent with these systems. Independent desktop Chromium browser tests with mobile emulation report successful runs with player displacement exceeding 109px, active game state changes, responsive touch start/move/cancel events, no failed resource loads, visible run identity, and upgrade menu interactions, evidencing interactive gameplay that includes the new mechanics. The launch overlay and HUD update reflect functional mobile controls and progression systems. All acceptance criteria requested for playable preview and multi-subsystem gameplay are supported by entered evidence. The implementation maintains existing mobile controls and progression compatibility with no deployment or QA approval claims, appropriate for pre-publication preview approval.
objections: Physical-device testing and human enjoyment feedback remain unverified due to environment restrictions; thus playability on all devices or long-run fun remain pending publisher steps.

Private player feedback video ingestion and transcript integration in roadmap handoff remain incomplete and unverified by the coder, limiting confirmation that implemented gameplay fully matches evolving player suggestions.
Performance impact under heavy load on lower-end mobiles and UI clutter risk are noted mitigation areas and remain empirically unmeasured in the current evidence.
No direct evidence proves comprehensive visual animation fidelity or accessibility optimizations across all supported devices; only implementation logic and desktop emulation are demonstrated.

# Cataclysm 0.8 implementation report

Implemented all selected candidates together: **designer**, **researcher**, **engineer**. Edited only `docs/preview/index.html`, `game.js`, `game.css` and this report. Configuration, dependencies, tests, metadata, publishing code and frozen v0.7 source were not edited. No deployment or independent QA approval is claimed.

## Inputs and evidence boundary

Read `artifacts/mobile/job.json`, `plan.json` (including `update_decision.selection`), `feedback.md` (empty array), `game_factory/CATACLYSM_1_0_ROADMAP.md`, and the existing HTML/CSS/JS. The supplied binding Council decision selects all three systems. This Coder did not access private footage, speech or an authenticated playback stage; only the prior evidence analyst inspected that material. This report does not independently certify ingestion of the complete recording. The roadmap still describes ingestion as pending; that discrepancy cannot be resolved from the supplied public files. No private dialogue is reproduced.

## Selected implementation and contracts

### designer — Beacon of Aid

`Beacon`, `deployBeacon`, `updateSupport`, `upgradeAvailable`, `chooseUpgrade`, `renderWorld` and `updateHud` implement actual placed entities in `game.beacons`. Each has world x/y, type, radius 150, duration 15, remaining life and an update method. Level 3/6/9 milestone menus unlock fire/heal/magnet choices respectively; subsequent milestones retain unlocked choices. Picking a beacon upgrade grants two charges (stock cap three) and deploys one at the cat's current position. A collapsible Support panel offers an accessible aura select and a 44px deployment button for later charges. Two simultaneous beacons maximum; menu options disable at capacity. Deployment is otherwise allowed only while running. Restart clears charges and zones.

Zones render with restrained translucent fill, boundary, type and countdown. Only the player's location within a zone grants its buff. Local enemies within a zone plus 100px move 8% faster, adding pressure without extra spawns. Charges require upgrade investment rather than unlimited deployment.

### researcher — Companion Familiar

`summonCompanion(type)` and `updateCompanion(dt)` replace the single-role pet logic. `game.activeCompanion` contains one entity, role, rank, duration/life, position, flash and attack clock. The existing `game.entities.petCompanion` references that same entity to preserve legacy gas avoidance, rendering and diagnostics. The old Pet companion upgrade remains functional and summons a shooter with its original pick-budget rules.

New role choices unlock on level 3/6/9 milestones: shooter follows and fires faster/harder; healer follows behind with regeneration within 180px; tank moves between cat and nearest threat and mitigates damage within 180px. Every role has independent supporting fire unaffected by the player's ghost silence. Summoning replaces the previous familiar. Duration scales from 35s with level (level contribution capped at 20s) and training (+5s/rank); damage and cooldown also scale with capped level/rank contributions. Each role has three training ranks. Role choices disable at rank cap and below unlock level. Companion expiration clears both references.

### engineer — Feral Instinct

`game.feralInstinct` tracks active, timer, six-second duration and an armed flag. `updateSupport` counts living enemies within 100 world pixels. Three activate +30% movement speed and +25% damage; fewer do not. An orange player outline, persistent status text with countdown, and activation/expiration notices explain the effect. Leaving the crowd rearms it after expiration, preventing indefinite immediate retrigger while stationary inside a swarm. Permanent player stats are never multiplied in place.

### Shared integration

`tick(dt)` updates support timers/effective stats before gas/contact damage, companion AI and player movement/fire. All timers and regeneration use simulation seconds; the existing running-mode guard freezes them during pause and upgrades. Input is cleared on upgrade and pause, and the original keyboard, pointer capture, release/cancel and Samsung fallback handlers remain intact.

Central `game.effectiveBuffs` defines additive bonuses and caps: fire multiplier <=1.7, pickup bonus <=180px, combined regeneration <=0.3 HP/s, damage mitigation <=40%, damage multiplier <=2.5. Rage adds +100% and Feral +25% (together 2.25x); Feral movement is 1.3x. These apply to real movement, projectiles, pickup attraction, healing and damage. Tank mitigation covers contact and gas. Fractional HP is displayed rounded upward to one decimal rather than printing a long floating point value.

The UI overlay contract uses the existing upgrade dialog, a separate collapsible Support details panel, `support-status`, and existing notices. No parallel overlay framework was needed. Specials remain scrollable on small screens; under-level support choices are hidden, capped choices disabled. Companion colors/rings distinguish roles; beacon circles and feral outline do not animate, respecting reduced motion. No external graphics, network services or dependencies added.

Read-only `CATACLYSM_DIAGNOSTICS.snapshot()` preserves existing fields and adds detached copies of beacons, charges, active companion, role ranks, Feral state, effective buffs and support upgrade availability. No test controls or mutation hooks were added to shipped code. Version/boot checks now agree on 0.8; `game-version` remains present. The current run label is visible in HTML.

## Reconciliation, dependencies and deliberate tuning

Existing systems retained: automatic combat, spread/ricochet/pickup upgrades, fish/XP and sequential upgrade resolution, persistent best/run progression, night difficulty, bosses, orbiter/stalker/ghost enemies, ghost silence, gas, power crates, music/mute, edge escape shield and reduced motion. Existing special-pick budget remains four; new support training uses independent caps so exhausting the old budget cannot block the new late milestones.

Dependency chain: milestone menu/availability -> charges or role ranks -> bounded support entities -> centralized effective buffs -> actual movement/fire/pickups/damage -> visual/status/diagnostics. All selected source operations are integrated, rather than separately applied patches.

Concrete tuning beyond the suggested pseudocode: finite beacon stock, three-rank role training, rearm-after-escape for Feral, explicit additive caps and modest local beacon pressure. No selected subsystem is deferred. Boss spawning now replaces one ordinary enemy if at the existing population cap, preventing bosses from exceeding the total cap; otherwise the difficulty/director logic is preserved.

## Checks actually executed

- `node --check docs/preview/game.js` — PASS, including after final changes.
- `git diff --check` — PASS.
- `node /tmp/cataclysm_integration.cjs` — PASS after final changes. This temporary Node VM harness loads the actual shipped JS, supplies DOM stubs, and exposes internal functions only in its in-memory test copy; shipped diagnostics remain read-only. No repository tests were changed. Coverage: level gates at 3/6/9; menu freeze of time/HP; upgrade/deploy at actual position; charge and two-zone bounds; local fire buff and loss outside zone; 15s removal; three companion roles, scaling, rank caps, replacement/expiry and shots during player silence; healer regeneration and tank mitigation; Feral two-vs-three threshold, exact multiplier, expiration and crowd rearm; actual projectile damage with Rage; overlapping healing/fire caps; pause preserving all support timers; fresh restart; rising existing difficulty, ghost/stalker/orbiter tiers, regular/boss total population bounds, and detached diagnostic copies.
- The same harness ran 3,600 actual ticks (60 simulated seconds) with initial 95-enemy population, two beacons and tank active together. Final run mean tick 0.1034ms, p95 0.1748ms, maximum 0.6981ms on this host. Population stayed <=95, time advanced, zones expired, and permanent speed stayed unchanged. These are CPU simulation measurements with DOM stubs, not browser rendering/FPS or mobile-device measurements. Timing checks were repeated only after a final ordering/damage-message change.
- `curl -I http://127.0.0.1:8765/preview/` — no supplied HTTP server was listening.
- `python -m http.server 8765 --directory docs` — blocked by sandbox `PermissionError: Operation not permitted` while creating a socket.
- `node game_factory/mobile_acceptance.cjs` — attempted; unable to execute gameplay. Chromium crashed before opening a page with crashpad `setsockopt: Operation not permitted` / SIGTRAP. The suite itself was not altered. No browser/mobile control acceptance pass is claimed; runner must execute it independently in its supplied environment. No gate.log from an earlier failed attempt existed.

## Remaining ledger / following roadmap cycle

| Idea or uncertainty | Existing state / disposition |
| --- | --- |
| Richer familiar support | Implemented this release; multi-role design is Council extrapolation, not verified direct player request. Long-session balance remains unverified. |
| Tactical beacons and reactive crowd boost | Implemented this release; playtest positioning/charge balance and sustained survival impact still require measurement. |
| Enemy variety, music | Already present; preserved rather than reimplemented from viewer suggestions. |
| Emergency action when surrounded | Viewer proposal; Feral provides a reactive escape/combat boost but no manual area attack. Manual attack remains deferred. |
| Meaningful building collision | Deferred viewer suggestion; requires collision/pathfinding/performance work, not selected. Buildings remain scenery. |
| Health bar beside cat | Deferred viewer suggestion; current external HP feedback preserved, including fractional healing/guard values. |
| Smoothed power-gated threat unlocks | Roadmap hypothesis; deferred. Existing night/level gates preserved. Needs rolling effectiveness measurements, hysteresis and recovery policy first. |
| Population/threat-budget director | Roadmap hypothesis; deferred beyond total population bound. Current time-based spawn delay and cap preserved. |
| Long-run instrumentation, TTK, DPS, recovery pacing | Deferred comprehensive instrumentation; current simulation checks cover difficulty increase, tier access and spawn bounds, not the full survival curve. |
| Later encounters, environmental changes, surprise events | Deferred pending evidence-specific selection and dependency tests. No invented quantitative survival target. |
| Exhaustive timestamped recording ledger | Not reconstructable from supplied public Council proposals; must remain in the authorized private evidence workflow. No unsupplied timestamps or footage claims. |
| Combined mobile UI/performance and balance | Browser rendering, touch regression, physical phones, long-run human outcomes and visual clarity remain unverified here due environment restrictions. Independent acceptance is still required. |

No changes were made to the living roadmap or frozen baseline. Pending items above are proposals/uncertainties, not newly verified playtest bugs.
